title: Video Editing — Practical Assessment
description: Movie / TV Series Character Edit — Video Editing & Motion Graphics. Portrait 9:16, MP4, 30-60 seconds.
instructions:
PROJECT: Movie / TV Series Character Edit
CATEGORY: Video Editing & Motion Graphics
FORMAT: MP4
ORIENTATION: Portrait (9:16)
DURATION: 30-60 seconds

1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

For this assessment, you are required to create a cinematic and engaging edit using clips from your favourite movie or television series.

You have the creative freedom to choose any movie or series you enjoy. However, your edit must revolve around one or two major characters from your chosen movie or series.

The objective is to demonstrate your understanding of video editing, motion, timing, effects, transitions, and visual storytelling.

2. EDITING CONCEPT

Your video should begin with a relatively normal playback of a scene from your selected movie or series.

Allow viewers to experience the scene as it originally plays out. Avoid introducing heavy effects, transitions, or excessive editing at the beginning.

As your chosen soundtrack builds towards its major beat or musical impact, that is where your actual character edit should begin.

At this point, introduce your spotlight character or characters with creative editing techniques, effects, transitions, and beat-synchronised cuts.

Important: Your entire edit should revolve around your selected character(s). They should be the central focus of the video, not just random characters appearing throughout the edit.

3. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

The following techniques are expected to feature in your edit:

A. Speed Graph / Velocity Editing
- Make use of speed graphs to create smooth and intentional speed changes.
- Experiment with speed ramps, acceleration, and deceleration.
- Ensure your speed changes complement the movement and energy of your clips.
- Avoid abrupt or poorly executed speed changes.

B. Visual Effects
- Incorporate appropriate visual effects to enhance your footage.
- Explore effects that complement the mood, action, and personality of your chosen character.
- Avoid excessive effects that make the video look cluttered.

C. Transitions
- Use clean, smooth, and creative transitions.
- Your transitions should connect scenes naturally.
- Explore different transition techniques where necessary, ensuring they complement the soundtrack.

D. Dynamic Captions
- Incorporate dynamic captions into your edit.
- Your captions should have a clean, professional, After Effects-like appearance.
- Pay attention to typography, animation, positioning, timing, and readability.
- Captions should complement the video rather than distract from it.

E. Soundtrack & Beat Synchronisation
- Select your own soundtrack.
- Your editing should follow the rhythm, beats, and major impacts of your chosen soundtrack.
- Ensure that cuts, transitions, effects, and character introductions align with the music.
- Pay attention to the overall flow and rhythm of your edit.

4. BONUS REQUIREMENT: CAMERA TRACKING (+10 POINTS)

Camera tracking is optional but highly encouraged.

If you successfully incorporate camera tracking into your edit, you will receive an additional 10 bonus points.

You can explore creative ways to integrate tracked text, graphics, or other visual elements into your footage.

The camera tracking must be properly executed and should look naturally integrated into the scene.

This is an opportunity to earn additional points beyond your regular assessment score.

Note: Camera tracking is not compulsory. A well-executed edit without camera tracking can still earn an excellent score.

5. VIDEO QUALITY & ASSET REQUIREMENTS

Video quality is an important part of this assessment.
- Source your movie or series clips in HD quality.
- Avoid blurry, pixelated, or heavily compressed footage.
- Ensure that your final export is clean and visually sharp.
- Pay attention to colour consistency and overall footage quality.
- Ensure that your soundtrack and other audio elements are clear.

Your video will be assessed partly on its visual clarity. Poor-quality source footage will affect your overall presentation and score.

6. PERSONAL BRANDING

Every editor is required to create an original personal logo for this assessment.

Your video must close with your logo as the final screen.

You have two options:
- Create a static logo outro.
- Create an animated logo outro.

You are free to explore your own logo concept, typography, animation style, and presentation.

Ensure that your logo outro is clean, professional, and properly integrated into the video.

7. ASSESSMENT CRITERIA

- Speed Graph / Velocity Editing: 20
- Effects & Visual Enhancement: 15
- Transitions & Smoothness: 15
- Dynamic Captions: 10
- Beat Synchronisation & Timing: 15
- Storytelling & Character Focus: 10
- Video Quality & Clarity: 10
- Logo Design & Outro: 5
- TOTAL: 100

Bonus: Properly executed camera tracking earns an additional 10 points.

8. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Submit the following:
1. Your completed video edit in MP4 format.
2. Your original personal logo.
3. The editable project file.

Recommended duration: 30-60 seconds.
Orientation: 9:16 (1080 x 1920 pixels).

Because video and project files are large, submit them as links (Google Drive, Dropbox, WeTransfer or similar) rather than uploads. Set the sharing so the academy can view or download them, and use the response box below to explain your concept, your chosen character(s), and the techniques you used.

9. FINAL INSTRUCTIONS

- Choose a movie or series you genuinely enjoy.
- Select your character(s) carefully and make them the centre of your edit.
- Download high-quality footage before beginning.
- Research editing references and techniques before starting your project.
- Be intentional with your soundtrack selection.
- Make every transition, effect, speed change, and caption serve a purpose.
- Prioritise smoothness, precision, creativity, and visual storytelling.

Remember, this is not just about putting effects on clips. We want to see your ability to take existing footage and transform it into an engaging visual experience through creative editing.

Let your creativity speak. Good luck!
